It's not windows security stuff, it's windows privacy stuff. You should google whatever distro you have decided on in order to confirm it does not have its own privacy pitfalls. For actual security issues, do basically the same.

Dual booting can offer segmentation of your data which can offer another level of security/loop to hop thru. If you plan on having a wintendo partition for gaming only, and do everything else in linux, windows will not have access to your linux partitions unless you have used a windows friendly file system such as fat32. While its possible that someone could hack your windows system, poke around, install software to make the other partitions accessible, and access you data you will be hard pressed to find anyone who this has actually happened to IRL.

Were this a concern of mine, I would dual boot differently; via the bios. Check your bias boot options. I would suggest having different physical drives for linux and windows, and only enabling the drive with the OS you want to use when booting, unless you need temp access between them. If windows is compromised it wont matter. I mean, it's possible someone could hack the bios, enable a drive, and somehow windows not crash or require a reboot... But I dont think we are gonna see that happening outside of some good detective writing.

What ever choices you make, do not believe for 1 moment that using linux protects you. You MUST stay up to date on patches, and news feeds, and so on in order to make certain your OS, and the programs you decide to run, have had their security verified continuously. Failure to do this is why there are linux machines in the botnet. Users switch and smuggly think they are protected, become owned, and never even know it.
